description_full: Broadcom Inc. designs, develops, and supplies various semiconductor devices and infrastructure software solutions internationally. The company operates in two segments: Semiconductor Solutions and Infrastructure Software. The company offers networking connectivity, such as custom silicon solutions, ethernet switching & routing, ethernet NIC controllers, physical layer devices, and fiber optic components; wireless device connectivity, including RF semiconductor devices, connectivity solutions, custom touch controllers, and inductive charging ASICS; servers and storage system solutions, such as PCIE switches, SAS & raid products, fibre channel products, and HDD & SSD solutions; broadband solutions, includes set-top box, and broadband access; and industrial. The company also offers a private cloud software portfolio, including the VMware Cloud Foundation, Edge, vSphere foundation, telco cloud platform, private AI, live recovery, application networking and security, application development and data services; mainframe software, such as AIOPS & automation, database & data management, DEVX & DEVOPS, cybersecurity & compliance management, beyond code programs, foundational & open mainframe solutions; cybersecurity, such as endpoint, network, information, application security, and identity & access management; enterprise software; and fc san management. Its products are used in various applications in enterprise and data center networking, including artificial intelligence networking and connectivity, home connectivity, set-top boxes, broadband access, telecommunication equipment, wireless device and base stations, data center servers and storage systems, factory automation, power generation and alternative energy systems, and electronic displays. Broadcom Inc. was founded in 1961 and is headquartered in Palo Alto, California.

financial_summary: Broadcom Inc. is a mega-cap technology business with a $1.7T market cap on $63.9B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +24% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +2.2pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.

Returns on capital run at 20% against a 12% cost of capital, a 8-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it. Gross margins of 62% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $26.9B in free cash flow — roughly 42 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.19× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.9× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 7.9×.

Shareholder yield is only 0.8%, a thin return of capital, and stock-based comp at 12% of revenue is silent dilution an owner has to account for, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and within its sector the business captures 1.7× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

sect: Its 40% operating margin runs 33pp above the Technology median (7%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It captures 1.70x its revenue share in sector profits, taking a disproportionate slice of the profit pool.
It accounts for 1.4% of sector revenue and 2.5% of sector operating profit.
Over five years it has been gaining share of the sector profit pool (+24.0% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 533 companies in the universe; the top four hold 29% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares have drifted higher, up 6% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has pulled back 13% over the last three months.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 30% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 48% and a beta of 1.61, it amplifies market moves, though its beta has shifted (1y 3.10 vs 5y 1.88), so read it loosely.
Liquidity is deep, with about $8.0B traded a day.
In past sell-offs it fell 48% in the 2020 crash and 35% in the 2022 bear market.
val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $176 (margin of safety -97%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 22%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $74.72 to $394 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks expensive against Technology peers: P/E 44.3 vs 27.4, EV/EBITDA 34.0 vs 17.1 and P/FCF 61.5 vs 26.1 (sector median).
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 90% above its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 1.6% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 1.4% (vs the 8% bar).
The 47 covering analysts target $533 on average, 54% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 20% clears the cost of capital of 12.0% by 8pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.54).
It runs a 62% gross margin and converts 42% of revenue into free cash flow, or 30% after stock compensation.
Earnings quality looks solid: a Piotroski score of 8/9 and cash conversion of 1.19x.
ROE of 28% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (2.1x equity multiplier).
Operating margin is running 10pp above its own historical average, a peak-margin risk if conditions normalise.
It spends 17.2% of revenue on R&D and 11.8% on stock compensation (above the 2% gate).
hlth: Leverage is moderate at 1.9x net debt to EBITDA ($16.2B of cash against $65.1B of debt), above the 1.5x gate, with interest covered 7.9x.
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 12.1, in the safe zone).
Goodwill makes up 57% of assets, a soft asset exposed to impairment.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 24.4% over 3 years and 21.7% over 5 years, so growth is accelerating, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 12%).
At current returns, reinvesting 40% of profits supports about 8.0% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Free cash flow has compounded 18.3% a year over five years.
Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 1.20 (orders outpacing sales), a backlog worth 52% of annual revenue and deferred revenue down 10%.
Capex roughly matches depreciation (1.1x, 1.0% of sales), a maintenance pace.
own: Insiders own a modest 1.9%, and institutions hold 79%.
Insider trading is two-way: 1 purchase and 69 sales over the past year, net $533.3M sold.
Shareholder yield is a modest 0.8% (0.1% in buybacks and 0.7% in dividends).
The share count has grown 2.9% a year over five years, diluting existing holders.
It has paid a dividend for 15 consecutive years, raising it 16.3% a year over the last five.
people: With about 33,000 employees, each generates about $1.9M of revenue, 5.2x the Technology median, and revenue has grown 17.3% a year across its filed history.
That works out to $816K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $2.9M (2x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores poorly (10/10, lower is better).
